entries.authors: Zhuoning Xu, Xiucheng Zhang, Hanjun Luo, Yingbin Jin, Yinpeng Dong, Hanan Salam

Differentiation: MasDrift measures loss of authorization boundaries (workers doing more than permitted) and treats showing the root request as a defense; our study plants an explicit instruction-versus-objective conflict and measures whether hierarchy visibility makes the worker depart from its literal instruction toward the parent objective, announced or silent, with length-matched and hierarchy-matched controls and reasoning-token accounting. Differentiation: Their manipulation is the handoff artifact's length and constraint explicitness, and the outcome is privacy leakage past a boundary rule; ours holds the worker's instruction fixed and adds layers of hierarchy context above it, measuring objective-directed departure and flagging. They show rules degrade in transit; we show what the worker does when the rule and the objective visibly disagree. Gist: Handoff summaries between agents preserve operational facts but weaken the boundary metadata governing how facts may be used, a failure the authors call summary collapse; on GPT-5-mini and DeepSeek-R1-32B, boundary-marker survival is near-uncorrelated with fact survival, and a 25-word budget drops it from about 0.80 to about 0.57. Downstream leakage depends on boundary explicitness (vague constraints leak in 73 percent of GPT and 50 percent of DeepSeek cases, explicit ones under 15 percent), a single-agent no-handoff control leaks more than the operationalized handoff, and an audience allowlist nearly eliminates leakage.

Their capability trend runs in the opposite direction from ours, which is a contrast to explain rather than an overlap. Gist: Defines the collaboration tax as the team-decentralisation loss of a two-player cooperative game with private information and measures it on 32 solo-tractable tasks across 11 models from 7 providers. Evaluates them in MemClaw, a production multi-tenant memory service, via the ArgusFleet harness, reporting 100% depth-four provenance reconstruction, high intra-fleet visibility with zero cross-fleet leakage, and two production enforcement defects.

Analytical rather than empirical, focused on the memory-constraint and noise-management interplay.

entries.title: When Attention Closes: How LLMs Lose the Thread in Multi-Turn Interaction
entries.authors: Dongre, Vardhan; Hsieh, Joseph; Lai, Viet Dac; Yoon, Seunghyun; Bui, Trung; Hakkani-Tür, Dilek
entries.use: Cite as the mechanistic reason a single objective sentence (V1) placed early may fail to steer while a verbatim brief (V2) does: attention accessibility of goal tokens, not their presence, governs goal-conditioned behavior. Also supports the interpretation that hierarchy context raises reasoning tokens by keeping goal tokens attended.
entries.verification_source: arXiv abs page (v1, 13 May 2026)
entries.note: Web sweep 2026-09-03 (WebSearch, WebFetch, arXiv API, Crossref). Threat: adjacent. Differentiation: Single-agent multi-turn mechanism study with open-weight models and attention probes; the visibility study is a behavioral single-turn delegation experiment on API models where the goal is supplied at varying depths of hierarchy, not lost over turns. Gist: Proposes a channel-transition account of multi-turn degradation: goal-defining tokens become less accessible via attention while goal information may persist in residual representations, measured with a Goal Accessibility Ratio (GAR), sliding-window ablations and residual probes. A causal ablation in Mistral that force-closes the attention channel drops 20-fact recall to 11% and raises persona-constraint violations; probes recover recall outcomes with AUC up to 0.99 across four architectures.

entries.title: Prompt Infection: LLM-to-LLM Prompt Injection within Multi-Agent Systems
entries.authors: Lee, Donghyun; Tiwari, Mo

Silent propagation is the attack outcome there; silent deviation is the null finding here. Gist: Introduces Prompt Infection, an LLM-to-LLM prompt injection that self-replicates across interconnected agents like a computer virus, enabling data theft, scams, misinformation and system-wide disruption while propagating silently. Shows MAS are highly susceptible even without full communication sharing and proposes LLM Tagging as a defense that significantly reduces spread when combined with existing safeguards.

Evaluation across frameworks, communication structures and applications shows LLM-MAS are vulnerable to communication-channel attacks.

entries.title: ACIArena: Toward Unified Evaluation for Agent Cascading Injection

ARGUS cuts attack success from 28.8% to 3.8% while keeping 87.5% clean utility.

entries.title: Architecture Matters for Multi-Agent Security
entries.authors: Ben Hagag, William L. Anderson, Christian Schroeder de Witt, Sarah Scheffler
entries.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.MA; cs.CR; cs.LG), submitted 25 Apr 2026

Also supports the paper's claim that harness defaults on cross-agent context are a design variable with measurable consequences.

entries.note: Web sweep 2026-09-03 (WebSearch, WebFetch, arXiv API, Crossref). Threat: adjacent. Their independent variable overlaps ours (context visibility) but their dependent variable is attack success, not objective-directed departure. Gist: Empirical study of how multi-agent design choices (agent roles, communication topology, memory/context visibility) trade off task performance against attack resistance across browser, desktop and code environments and 13 configurations, with stagewise evaluation from planning refusal to full attack completion. Multi-agent architectures are more vulnerable than standalone agents in most configurations, attack success varies by up to 3.8x, and no single design is universally safer.

entries.title: Agent Data Injection Attacks are Realistic Threats to AI Agents
entries.authors: Woohyuk Choi, Juhee Kim, Taehyun Kang, Jihyeon Jeong, Luyi Xing, Byoungyoung Lee
entries.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.CR; cs.AI), submitted 6 Jul 2026; comments: 19 pages, 19 figures, 7 tables

entries.note: Web sweep 2026-09-03 (WebSearch, WebFetch, arXiv API, Crossref). Threat: adjacent. Complementary threat model, not overlapping measurement. Gist: Introduces agent data injection (ADI), a category of indirect prompt injection where malicious content is disguised as trusted data such as resource identifiers, data origins, or tool-call and response formats, so agents act on attacker-controlled data without any injected instruction. Demonstrates real vulnerabilities in web agents (Claude in Chrome, Antigravity, Nanobrowser) and coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI), showing current agents do not isolate trusted from untrusted data.

entries.title: ASIDE: Architectural Separation of Instructions and Data in Language Models
entries.authors: Egor Zverev, Evgenii Kortukov, Alexander Panfilov, Alexandra Volkova, Soroush Tabesh, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Wojciech Samek, Christoph H. Lampert

Gist: Proposes ASIDE, an architectural element that separates instructions from data at the token-embedding level by applying an orthogonal rotation to data-token embeddings, adding no parameters. Instruction-tuning with ASIDE raises instruction-data separation without performance loss and improves robustness on prompt-injection benchmarks even without dedicated safety training.

entries.title: Authorization Propagation in Multi-Agent AI Systems: Identity Governance as Infrastructure
entries.authors: Krti Tallam

Claims identity governance must be infrastructure enforced at every interaction boundary, with preliminary evidence from an enterprise platform that ordinary (non-adversarial) behavior already produces the predicted failures.

entries.title: MESA: Prioritizing Vulnerable Communication Channels for Securing Multi-Agent Systems

harnesses.name: Claude Code agent teams (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS; lead + teammates; shared task list; mailbox; SendMessage)
harnesses.default_visibility: Parent conversation: NONE. A teammate is a full separate Claude Code session: 'Each teammate has its own context window. When spawned, a teammate loads the same project context as a regular session: CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, and skills. It also receives the spawn prompt from the lead. The lead's conversation history does not carry over.' Parent objective reaches the teammate only if the lead writes it into the spawn prompt (best-practice section: 'Include task-specific details in the spawn prompt'). Claude launches a teammate 'when it calls the Agent tool with a name while agent teams are enabled', so the spawn prompt is the Agent tool's `prompt` field. Teammates from a subagent definition get its body appended to the default system prompt (in-process) or in place of it (split pane); `skills` and (in-process) `mcpServers` fields are ignored and loaded from project/user settings instead. Messages arriving over SendMessage are labelled as coming 'from another Claude session, not from you', and a relayed approval claim is treated as untrusted. Requires an interactive session: with -p or the Agent SDK 'Claude doesn't spawn teammates, and a subagent that Claude names runs as an ordinary subagent'. Teammates inherit the lead's permission mode and effort level; plan-mode teammates work read-only until the lead session auto-approves their plan ('without the lead reviewing it'). Returned to parent: Final answer only, via an idle notification: 'when a teammate finishes and stops, it automatically notifies the lead and includes its final answer in the notification. A teammate whose turn ends on an API error notifies the lead that it failed and includes the error text.' Messages between agents are 'delivered automatically to recipients. The lead doesn't need to poll for updates.' Shutdown requests can be approved or rejected 'with an explanation'. Teammate transcripts are visible to the human (agent panel, Enter opens the transcript; split panes) but there is no documented path for the lead model to read a teammate transcript. Teammate permission prompts surface in the lead session for the human. Siblings or ledger: Highest sibling visibility of any Claude Code surface, but all opt-in through tools rather than injected context. (1) Shared task list: 'agents that have the Task tools can see task status and claim available work'; states pending/in progress/completed with dependencies; 'Task claiming uses file locking to prevent race conditions when multiple teammates try to claim the same task simultaneously'; stored at ~/.claude/tasks/{team-name}/ (persists; team config at ~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/config.json is removed at session end). Task tools are absent by default on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5 unless CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1 or --allowedTools/--tools name them (tools-reference); without them 'an agent coordinates with its team through messages instead of the shared task list'. (2) Roster: the team config 'contains a members array with each member's name and agent ID ... Teammates can read this file to discover other team members'; plus the sub-agents page sibling roster system reminder listing `main` and every named agent (v2.1.206+, only when tools include SendMessage). (3) Mailbox: per-agent JSON at ~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/inboxes/{agent-name}.json; 'any teammate can message any other by that name'; no broadcast: 'To reach everyone, send one message per recipient.' harnesses.default_visibility: Provider-dependent, and the model-facing tool wording is derived from the provider's `inheritsParentContext` flag. spawn (in-process, default example in the tool README): 'The child starts with an empty conversation, so a task prompt must stand alone'; 'The fresh child receives the task content verbatim as its only user message in a new empty conversation, with the parent provider, model, reasoning effort, output-token limit, and working directory by default'; 'No parent conversation message is included'. Tool description the model sees under spawn/acp: 'The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation.' fork (in-process): 'seeds each child with the parent's completed conversation turns: the child sees every finished turn and none of the in-flight one'; the seed is 'a balanced completed-turn prefix of the parent's log — the parent's events up to and including its last turn/end'; 'The seed is captured once at start; later parent turns never reach the child'; the tool wording becomes 'it does not see the current in-flight turn'. acp (out-of-process, any ACP-compatible agent): 'the child gets its own runtime, session, model configuration, and tools'; 'the parent supplies only the task and the working directory'; 'ACP reads only its cwd'. Codex and Claude Code product providers also exist (dsh-subagent-codex, dsh-subagent-claude-code) and, like ACP, 'reject agentOptions before starting their transports'. The subsystem doc states the flag values outright: '`inheritsParentContext` describes only conversation seeding (`fork`: true; `spawn` and `acp`: false)'. Parent task: nothing beyond the delegation `prompt` (SubagentStartRequest.prompt = 'Content delivered as the child's user message'); no objective or brief field exists in the schema (`description` is a 3-5 word display label). Returned to parent: Final output only. Tool description: 'The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps.' One-shot `SubagentResult` carries `output` (final assistant text), optional `structured` (when `outputSchema` was satisfied), `stopReason` (completed \| max-tokens \| refusal \| aborted \| error) and an optional sanitized `diagnostic` capped at 4096 UTF-8 bytes from which providers 'remove tool inputs, file contents, environment values, credentials, and raw protocol payloads'; a non-completed stop reason maps to an `isError` tool result rather than partial success. ACP: 'The parent receives only the child's final answer or a safe error — no intermediate messages or tool traffic crosses the boundary.' Background one-shot returns 'started background subagent job <id>' collected via `job_output`; continuable returns 'started subagent <childId>' and one settlement notice when the child's Activation ends. Observers (not the parent model) get paired `subagent/start` / `subagent/end` events and can enumerate children via `listChildren` / `listDescendants` without loading an agent. Siblings or ledger: No shared ledger. `send_message` is strictly adjacent: 'permits only a direct parent or direct continuable child'; 'Siblings, ancestors beyond one edge, self-targets, stale Agent objects, and one-shot children are rejected.' Delivered messages are framed 'Agent <sender-id> sent a message:' and 'provenance records the sender but grants no authority'. `list_agents` (separately loadable `/list-agents` plugin) shows the caller's continuable children with status running/idle/ready, not siblings. harnesses.name: Claude Code auto mode classifier at subagent handoffs (addition to the existing Claude Code sub-agents row)
harnesses.default_visibility: Not a visibility change for the worker; the post confirms the existing row's V0 framing from the safety side: 'Inside the subagent, the orchestrator's instruction is the user message, so tasks look fully authorized.' What the classifier itself sees: 'The classifier sees only user messages and the agent's tool calls; we strip out Claude's own messages and tool outputs, making it reasoning-blind by design'; it is a two-stage transcript classifier ('Stage 1 is a fast single-token (yes/no) filter instructed to err toward blocking; if it flags, stage 2 re-evaluates the same input with chain-of-thought reasoning'). Tiering: 'The transcript classifier sees everything else, including shell commands, web fetches, external tool integrations, subagent spawns, filesystem operations outside the project directory.' At delegation: 'The classifier runs at both ends of a subagent handoff: when work is delegated out and when results come back. The outbound check exists because, without it, the transcript classifier that monitors the subagent may not have the full context to know if the task it was given was originally intended by the user ... We catch it at delegation, while it's still recognizable as an agent choice rather than a user request.' Returned to parent: On return the classifier, not the parent model, reads the whole subagent transcript: 'The return check exists because a subagent that was benign at delegation could be compromised mid-run by a prompt injection in content it reads. Before results go back to the orchestrator, the classifier reviews the subagent's full action history. If it flags, we prepend a security warning for the agent that started the subagent rather than discard the results.' So the parent receives the subagent's result plus, when flagged, a prepended warning; the subagent's action history stays with the classifier. Siblings or ledger: Not addressed. The classifier is a per-handoff observer over one subagent's action history; nothing about sibling or ledger visibility.

harnesses.knob: Auto mode itself (the post positions it as replacing --dangerously-skip-permissions); deny-and-continue semantics when the classifier blocks. Siblings or ledger: Handoff: full shared memory and the state dict (e.g. research_notes, report_content, review) are visible to every agent.
